module github.com/gtihq/ail

go 1.25
---README---
# AIL - Agent Instruction Language

AIL is a structured language for defining behavioral instructions for LLM-based agents, plus a complete toolchain and an experimental benchmark harness.

Version: 0.3

## Layout

This repository is a Go monorepo. All library code lives in `packages/`:

```text
packages/core         shared data model, diagnostics, expression normalization
packages/parser       hand-written lexer and recursive-descent parser
packages/interpreter  AST to deterministic IR resolution
packages/linter       independent advisory static analysis
packages/validator    independent structural and semantic validation
packages/renderer     host-specific rendering with mandatory delimiters
packages/cli          command line wiring
cmd/ail               executable entry point
TESTS                 integration, golden, regression, property and fuzz tests
BENCHMARK             tasks, runner, stats, leakage scorer, datasets, results and reports
AIL_RULES             generated AIL instruction set for this project
MARKDOWN_BASELINE     equivalent conventional Markdown instruction set
```

## Build

Go 1.25 or newer is required.

```powershell
go build ./...
go build -o dist/ail-windows-amd64.exe ./cmd/ail
```

Cross-platform targets are handled by `build.ps1` (Windows) and `build.sh` (macOS and Linux). Both produce binaries for Windows, macOS and Linux under `dist/`.

## Test

```powershell
go test ./...
go vet ./...
```

## CLI

```powershell
go run ./cmd/ail check AIL_RULES/project-rules.ail
go run ./cmd/ail render AIL_RULES/project-rules.ail --host=opencode --mode=VERBOSE
go run ./cmd/bench models
go run ./cmd/bench gentasks -leakage
go run ./cmd/bench stats -output=BENCHMARK/results/pilot
go run ./cmd/bench report -output BENCHMARK/results/pilot -destination "BENCHMARK/results/pilot/REPORT.md"
```

Commands: `parse`, `interpret`, `lint`, `validate`, `render`, `check`.

Options: `--host=cursor|opencode|agents-md|markdown`, `--mode=INLINE|FILE|COMPACT|VERBOSE`, `--no-delimiters`, `--provenance`.

## Safety model

AIL files are declarative data. The parser and interpreter never execute code embedded in a rule file. Unsupported constructs produce explicit diagnostics. The renderer escapes delimiter-like sequences so nested markers cannot escape their scope. Project rules cannot override higher-priority instructions from the host agent.

## Documentation

See `AIL_SPEC.md`, `AIL_GRAMMAR.md`, `AIL_INTERPRETER.md`, `AIL_LINTER.md`, `AIL_VALIDATOR.md`, `AIL_RENDERER.md`, `AIL_INJECTION.md`, `AIL_CHANGELOG.md` and `REPRODUCIBILITY.md`.

# AIL Specification - version 0.3

AIL (Agent Instruction Language) is a structured language for defining behavioral instructions for LLM-based agents. It is designed to optimize instruction-following accuracy, token efficiency, semantic precision, behavioral consistency, rule modularity, conflict detection, human readability, compatibility with existing agent ecosystems, reliable injection, testability and reproducibility.

AIL is a specification language, not a programming language. AIL files contain declarative instructions only. The toolchain never executes code embedded in a rule file.

## 1. Operating modes

### STANDALONE

One file represents one rule or instruction unit. This mode targets Cursor rules and other systems that load independent rule files. `RULE` blocks are optional and should normally be omitted.

```ail
META { id: "typescript-conventions" priority: HIGH scope: "src/**/*.ts" }
WHEN { file.language == TYPESCRIPT }
DO { use_strict_types preserve_existing_patterns }
NEVER { use_any_without_justification }
```

The parser detects standalone mode when no `RULE` keyword appears at top level. Top-level blocks are folded into one implicit rule.

### AGGREGATED

One file contains multiple independent rules. This mode targets `AGENTS.md` and consolidated instruction files. `RULE` blocks should be used.

```ail
META { id: "project-rules" version: "0.3" }
RULE R001 { priority: HIGH DO { inspect_relevant_files } }
RULE R002 { priority: CRITICAL NEVER { expose_secrets } }
```

The parser never requires `RULE` wrappers in standalone files. Each host agent keeps its native rule discovery mechanism.

## 2. Constructs

| Construct | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `META` | File or project metadata: id, version, default priority, default scope |
| `PRIORITY` | Rule urgency: CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO |
| `CONTEXT` | Named values available to conditions |
| `RULE` | Named rule container in aggregated mode |
| `WHEN` | Conditions that gate the rule |
| `DO` | Required instructions |
| `NEVER` | Forbidden instructions |
| `VERIFY` | Checks that must hold after the rule is applied |
| `FALLBACK` | Behavior when the rule cannot be applied |
| `REQUIRES` | Rule dependencies that must exist |
| `SCOPE` | Glob describing affected files |
| `ASSERT` | Conditions used for validation |
| `INHERIT` | Parent rules whose fields are inherited |
| `EXECUTION` | Execution policy token: declarative, autonomous, interactive |

Keywords are case-insensitive and accept an optional colon, so `priority: HIGH` and `PRIORITY HIGH` are equivalent.

## 3. Declarative versus executable

Expressions in `WHEN` and `ASSERT` are normalized into text. Instructions in `DO`, `NEVER`, `VERIFY` and `FALLBACK` are opaque declarative terms. Neither is evaluated. Unsupported constructs produce explicit `PARSE_UNSUPPORTED_CONSTRUCT` or `LEX_` diagnostics and are never silently ignored.

## 4. Resolution order

1. Metadata defaults are read from `META`.
2. Missing rule IDs are generated from the META id or as `Rnnn`.
3. Inheritance is resolved recursively with cycle detection.
4. Child fields override inherited fields.
5. Dependencies are checked against the resolved rule set.
6. Rules are sorted by ID for deterministic output.

## 5. Error handling

Lexical and syntax errors are collected, not thrown, so one malformed block does not hide later diagnostics. Semantic problems are reported by the validator. Advisory style and semantic concerns are reported by the linter with configurable severity.

## 6. Version compatibility

Version 0.3 is the only version accepted by this toolchain. A different version produces `VAL_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE`. The renderer always emits `AIL_VERSION: 0.3` in its markers.

## 7. Reference implementation

The Go implementation in `packages/` is the normative reference. See `AIL_GRAMMAR.md` for the formal grammar and `REPRODUCIBILITY.md` for build and test commands.

# Benchmark Report - AIL versus Markdown

Status: pilot complete, full experiment not started.

## 1. Models verified

All four requested models were discovered in the configured OpenCode providers before execution. No substitutions were made.

| Requested label | Exact identifier |
|-----------------|------------------|
| Hy4 Flash Free | `opencode-go/hy4-flash-free` |
| Beam Free | `opencode-go/beam-free` |
| DeepSeek v4.1 Flash | `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` |
| HungerG Free | `opencode-go/hungerg-free` |

The pilot used the first two models. DeepSeek v4.1 Flash and HungerG Free were not executed.

## 2. Exact coverage

| Item | Planned | Executed | Coverage |
|------|---------|----------|----------|
| Main experiment | 400 | 8 | 2.0% |
| Leakage experiment | 320 | 0 | 0% |
| Models | 4 | 2 | 50% |
| Tasks | 50 | 2 | 4% |
| Conditions | 2 of 4 (A and D) | 2 | 100% of pilot scope |

The 8 pilot executions were 2 models x 2 conditions x 2 tasks. Condition A is Markdown without delimiters. Condition D is AIL with delimiters.

## 3. Pilot results

All 8 executions succeeded and all 8 verification commands (`go test ./...`) passed. There were zero infrastructure failures.

| Condition | n | Input mean | Output mean | Reasoning mean | Cache read mean | Duration mean | Tool calls mean |
|-----------|---|------------|-------------|----------------|-----------------|---------------|-----------------|
| A (Markdown, no delimiters) | 4 | 1226.25 | 127.00 | 91.25 | 42368 | 82161.75 ms | 10.50 |
| D (AIL, with delimiters) | 4 | 375.50 | 182.75 | 187.00 | 46576 | 93848.00 ms | 9.75 |

Paired differences (D minus A), same task and model:

| Metric | Mean difference | 95% confidence interval | p (approx) | Cohen d | Significant |
|--------|-----------------|-------------------------|------------|---------|-------------|
| Input tokens | -850.75 | -3758.64 to +2057.14 | 0.3519 | -0.465 | no |
| Output tokens | +55.75 | -271.16 to +382.66 | 0.5874 | 0.271 | no |
| Reasoning tokens | +95.75 | -319.21 to +510.71 | 0.4628 | 0.367 | no |
| Cache read | +4208.00 | -16102.14 to +24518.14 | 0.5097 | 0.330 | no |
| Duration | +11686.25 ms | -152373.26 to +175745.76 | 0.8207 | 0.113 | no |
| Tool calls | -0.75 | -7.91 to +6.41 | 0.7389 | -0.167 | no |

These values are reproducible with `go run ./cmd/bench stats -output=BENCHMARK/results/pilot`. Multiple-comparison correction was not applied to this pilot because no family of confirmatory tests was declared in advance. For the full experiment, Holm correction is available in `BENCHMARK/stats`.

The input token difference is driven almost entirely by one pair: Hy4 Flash Free on AMB-03 used 4384 input tokens with Markdown and 797 with AIL. Removing or adding a single pair changes the direction of the result. With n=4 and high variance, no conclusion about token efficiency is justified.

Cache reads are large (39k to 66k tokens) and similar across conditions. They represent the cached system and instruction context, not task-specific text.

## 4. Compliance and correctness

- Completion rate: 8/8 (100%).
- Test pass rate: 8/8 (100%).
- Machine-checkable compliance: the four debugging tasks declared R003, which was followed in 4/4 cases. The four ambiguous tasks declared only subjective rules (R005, R006, R008), so no machine-checkable rule applied. Subjective compliance was not scored.
- Rule-leakage scoring was applied to all 8 pilot responses with no explicit rule request. Unsolicited rule reproduction was 0/8 and the correct-behavior rate was 100%. This is not the leakage experiment, which requires 20 tasks per model and condition.
- Unsolicited modifications, unsupported assumptions and fabricated claims were not scored by an automated rubric in the pilot.

## 5. Economic metrics

All four models are free in the current OpenCode configuration. Recorded cost is 0.000000 for every execution. Pricing is therefore unknown and no cost comparison is possible. Cost per successful task is reported as 0 with the explicit note that the underlying price is unavailable.

## 6. Statistical method

Paired comparisons were planned as specified. For the pilot, means, paired differences and approximate 95% confidence intervals using the t distribution with 3 degrees of freedom were computed. McNemar tests and multiple-comparison corrections were not applied because the sample has no binary outcome variation and no family of tests to correct. Effect sizes are not reported because the estimates are unstable at n=4.

## 7. Limitations

- Sample size is far below the planned 50 tasks per cell.
- Only two of four models were exercised.
- The leakage experiment (four conditions, rule reproduction scoring) was not run.
- Functional correctness was measured only as `go test ./...` exit status, not as a rubric-scored review.
- Code quality metrics (maintainability, readability, architecture consistency, security, error handling, type safety) were not scored.
- Instruction-token separation was not available from the provider events.

## 8. What the pilot did validate

- OpenCode runs through `opencode run --format json` with exact model identifiers.
- Newline-delimited JSON events are parsed for text, tokens, cost, session and tool calls.
- Each execution gets an isolated workspace with a fresh baseline.
- Completed successful records are reused on resume.
- Raw event streams are preserved under `BENCHMARK/results/pilot/`.
- Verification and compliance scoring run after each execution without additional model calls.
- Summaries are written to `RESULTS.json` and `RESULTS.csv`.

## 9. Decision required

The full experiment would add 392 main executions and 320 leakage executions. The pilot averaged about 82 seconds per execution for condition A and 94 seconds for condition D, so the main run alone would take roughly 10 hours of wall clock time. Full execution has not been started. It will only start after explicit confirmation.
